title: Overlapping Network Community Detection Using Sparse Backbones
abstract: Community structures are common in real networks, and extracting them provides valuable insight in applications ranging from drug discovery to market segmentation. Overlapping community detection (OCD) is the task of clustering networked data in which nodes may belong to multiple clusters. Existing OCD algorithms often struggle to achieve a suitable balance between detection quality and scalability. We, therefore, propose Highway, a scalable OCD algorithm that exploits the sparse backbone of the input network to perform efficient community inference. We used 728 Lancichinetti-Fortunato-Radicchi benchmark networks to compare Highway and its ablated version against 10 existing OCD algorithms. Our results, based on five performance measures, demonstrate a competitive performance for Highway. It ranks first in overlapping normalized mutual information with a 6.9% improvement over the strongest baseline. It also ranks second in all the other four performance measures. These comparative results suggest that Highway coupled with its backbone procedure offers a suitable accuracy-efficiency trade-off. The Highway algorithm is open-source and available as part of the CDlib library.
summary: This paper introduces Highway, a novel and scalable algorithm for Overlapping Community Detection (OCD) that improves efficiency by utilizing the sparse backbone of an input network. By combining modularity and Jaccard scores to build this backbone, Highway accurately infers overlapping community structures. The method demonstrates superior performance across multiple metrics when tested against numerous benchmark networks.
main_problem: The core problem is Overlapping Community Detection (OCD) in complex networks, where nodes can belong to multiple clusters.
main_result: The proposed Highway algorithm achieves state-of-the-art performance on 728 benchmark networks, ranking first in overlapping normalized mutual information with a significant improvement over existing methods.
method: Highway is a scalable OCD algorithm that leverages the sparse backbone of the input network to perform efficient community inference through anchor initialization and neighbor propagation.
model_or_system: The system analyzed is general network data represented by a graph G=(V, E). The method constructs a sparse backbone H using a hybrid edge scoring function combining modularity and Jaccard overlap scores.
key_observables: Membership matrix (alpha), Pattern confidence score (gamma(P)), Calibration strength (lambda_v), Fuzzy Rand Index (FRI), overlapping modularity (Q_ov), Dice index, F*, and Overlapping Normalized Mutual Information (ONMI).
important_parameters: The backbone construction uses a hybrid weight $\omega$ for the edge scoring function. The final membership update involves tuning parameters like $ eta$, $\eta$, and $	au$.
main_assumptions: The method assumes that primary community signals propagate effectively through a limited set of structurally informative edges (the sparse backbone).
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem, details the Highway algorithm in stages: Backbone Construction, Anchor-based Signal Initialization, Neighbor-only Propagation, and final Anchor-Preserving Pattern Calibration. It concludes with extensive comparative results on benchmark networks.
why_interesting: While focused on network science rather than quantum physics directly, the underlying mathematical framework of community detection shares conceptual parallels with finding emergent structures or ground states in complex physical systems, which can sometimes be modeled using graph theory techniques relevant to condensed matter analysis.
